doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Passion and loving the work
summary: Rowe compares Parsons' varied gigs to Joe Wilder's and quotes Phil Woods; both agree you should only be a musician if you have to.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: You made it your business to know where the exits were, right? I love your description. It reminds me of fellas like Joe Wilder and the long trek through all these different kinds of gigs and developing a work ethic which is so important, and making yourself stand out so your phone rings.
Yeah, yes, yes. It’s a passion and someone who doesn’t love it shouldn’t mess with this.

Do you see that in your students? Does it occur to you – I remember Phil Woods said this thing, I’ll be very brief about it. He said you know if you’re thinking about being a jazz tenor player or a brain surgeon, be the brain surgeon and play tenor on the weekends.
Something you have to do is to be a musician. If you don’t have to then –
Do something else, that’s right. Do another thing.
